name: FromNarrative
title: Narrative Conformance Statements
description: Conformance statements found throughout the narrative of the IG consolidated into this computable resource for traceability purposes

statement.requirement: The PHG SHOULD specify a sufficiently selective conditional-create criterion so that at most one matching resource is found on the server.
When an equivalent UCUM code is known, this UCUM code SHALL be used.
An implementation SHALL use the MDC code if it does not know the UCUM code for the given unit.
The converted effective[x] SHALL retain fractional-second precision consistent with the PHD's tick resolution, so that time differences between observations are preserved.
A derived RR interval Observation SHOULD reference the source ECG waveform Observation using Observation.derivedFrom.
The MDC code SHALL be present in a coding element.

Because PHDs often have unreliably set clocks, a PHD that generates measurements with timestamps SHOULD provide a means for the PHG to determine the PHD's current time and clock status information, such as its synchronization state.
This measurement SHOULD contain a derived-from reference pointing to the measurement containing the glucose concentration.
For a PHD, Device.conformsTo SHALL contain at least one MDC specialization entry.
PHDs SHOULD use the unchanged timestamp of a generated observation as received from the PHD.
PHGs compliant with this IG SHOULD implement this identifier as specified to ensure this scheme works across all compliant gateways.
For device settings known to the PHG, Observation.subject SHOULD point to the PHD.
For Coincident Timestamp Observations, Observation.performer SHOULD NOT be provided.

Observations whose timestamps are neither from the PHD's current timeline nor from a timeline synchronized with an external time source SHOULD be discarded, since there is no way to give them a correct timestamp.

When the PHG modifies an Observation's timestamp as received from the PHD, it SHALL also generate a Coincident Timestamp Observation that records how the Observation.effective[x] element is generated.
When uploading to a FHIR server, the gateway SHOULD report the group observation with a hasMember reference to all member Observations.
In FHIR, the session Observation SHOULD have hasMember references to all observations that are part of the session.
PHGs SHALL include a category element with a fixed coding as specified by the profile.
Vital-sign Observations SHOULD include a category element as defined by the Vital Signs profile.
When encoding numeric Observation quantities in FHIR, the PHG SHOULD follow the precision indicated by the PHD's IEEE 11073 FLOAT or SFLOAT encoding.
However, if the PHD does not report a System-identifier, which may happen if one needs to map non-certified and/or proprietary devices, a transport address SHOULD be reported.
When a PHG encounters such a device it SHALL provide a transport address as a means of uniquely identifying the PHD.
The Accuracy attribute SHALL be reported if the PHD provides it.
Measurement-Confidence-95 SHALL be reported if the PHD provides it.
There SHALL be one coding element using the MDC coding system.
If the measurement is a vital sign, an additional coding element SHALL use a LOINC vital-sign code.
The PHG SHALL use a Patient.identifier supplied by the server when one is provided.
If the server does not provide an identifier, the PHG SHALL generate an implementation-dependent identifier whose value is unique within its assigning system.
The type for a PHG-generated identifier SHOULD use a suitable code from the HL7 v2-0203 coding system.

PHG implementers that generate device alerts SHOULD follow the two alert-generation pathways — threshold/limit alerts on numeric observations and device/sensor status-bit alerts — described in the PhdDeviceAlert profile.
Uploads generated by PHGs compliant to this IG SHALL use the mapping defined by this implementation guide when transforming PHD data to FHIR resources.
The PHG SHOULD implement a duplication detection mechanism and filter out any observations that have already been uploaded.
